en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn how to give good advice and talk about rules in English. Let's start!

steps.title: Good advice: should
steps.text: When you tell a friend *sebaiknya …*, English uses **should**.
steps.body:
Pattern: **should + base verb** (the verb as in the dictionary: no -s, no -ing, no to). **You should drink more water.** For a bad idea, use **shouldn't** (= should not): **You shouldn't stay up late.**
should is a helper word like *can*: it never changes, and nothing goes between it and the verb. So **she should go**, not 'she shoulds go' or 'she should to go'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari is very tired after a long day at the office. What's good advice for her?

options: Sari should to go to bed early.
Sari shoulds go to bed early.
Sari should go to bed early.
question.explanation: **should + base verb**: should go. There's no **to** after should, and should never takes -s, even with Sari (= she).

steps.title: Rules and duties: have to and must
steps.text: When something is **necessary** (*harus, wajib*), English uses **have to** or **must**.
steps.body:
**have to** + base verb changes like the verb *have* you know: **I / you / we / they have to**, but **he / she has to** (like *she has a car*). So 'she have to' is a mistake.
**must** + base verb never changes, like can: **I must, she must**, with no to after it.
Both mean *harus*. **have to** is the most common when you speak; **must** is common on signs and in written rules.

steps.title: have to or has to?
steps.text: Pak Hasan is a security guard at a bank in Surabaya.

question.prompt: Complete: Pak Hasan ___ work at night on Fridays.
question.explanation: Pak Hasan = he, so **has to** (like *he has*). 'have to' is for I / you / we / they, and there's never a **to** after must.

steps.title: Build the rule
steps.text: A new office has a rule for all visitors. The receptionist tells you the rule.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamu harus menunjukkan KTP-mu.
question.solution: You must show your ID card.
question.explanation: **must + base verb**, with no to: **You must show** … Then what you show: **your ID card**.

steps.title: mustn't or don't have to?
steps.text: Careful! In **negative** sentences, must and have to mean very different things.
steps.body:
**mustn't** (= must not) = *dilarang, tidak boleh*: there's a rule, or it's dangerous.
**don't have to** = *tidak perlu, tidak harus*: it isn't necessary, you can choose. With he / she: **doesn't have to** (not 'doesn't has to').
The trap: word by word, *tidak harus* looks like 'must not'. But **mustn't** means *dilarang*! *Tidak harus / tidak perlu* = **don't have to**.

steps.title: Not allowed or not necessary?
steps.text: Look at these pairs. Ask yourself: is it a rule, or just not needed?
steps.body: Rules, signs and danger → **mustn't**. Free things, holidays, choices → **don't / doesn't have to**.

examples.en: You mustn't use your phone in the exam.
You mustn't touch the cables. It's dangerous.
The seminar is free. You don't have to pay.
examples.id: Seminarnya gratis. Kamu tidak perlu bayar.

examples.en: Sari doesn't have to cook tonight. Her mother is cooking.
examples.id: Sari tidak perlu masak malam ini. Ibunya sedang masak.

examples.en: Come to my house on Sunday! You don't have to bring anything.
examples.id: Datang ke rumahku hari Minggu! Tidak usah bawa apa-apa.

steps.title: A free morning
steps.text: Rina works in an office from Monday to Friday. Today is Sunday.

question.prompt: It's Sunday. Rina ___ get up early today.
question.explanation: Getting up early isn't forbidden; it just isn't necessary today, so **doesn't have to**. Rina = she, so **doesn't**. 'mustn't' would mean she is not allowed to get up early.

steps.title: Read the sign
steps.text: You're at a swimming pool in Bandung. There's a sign on the wall: **NO RUNNING**.

options: You don't have to run here.
question.explanation: A sign with a rule means it's not allowed: **mustn't** (= dilarang). 'You don't have to run' only means running isn't necessary.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the English before you check.

flashcards.front: Correct it: Dimas have to study.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for the next time you give advice or read a sign!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · should, have to, must
artifact.intro: should = advice. have to / must = necessary. mustn't = not allowed. don't have to = not necessary.
rows: I / you / we / they have to + verb
We have to pay in cash.
Rina has to take the KRL.
The seminar is free. You don't have to pay.
Should I …? / Do I have to …?
Do I have to pay for parking? — Yes, you do.
tips: **No to** after should and must: You should rest. You must stop. (have to already has its to.)
**has to** with he / she / it, like *she has*; but **doesn't have to**, not 'doesn't has to'.
**tidak harus / tidak perlu = don't have to**. mustn't means *dilarang*.

examples.en: Should I bring a jacket? — Yes, you should.
examples.id: Sebaiknya saya bawa jaket? — Ya, sebaiknya.

examples.en: I must call my mother tonight.
examples.id: Saya harus menelepon ibu saya nanti malam.

examples.en: Come to my house on Sunday! You don't have to bring anything.
examples.id: Datang ke rumahku hari Minggu! Tidak usah bawa apa-apa.

steps.title: Watch and practise
steps.text: Want more? Watch a short video about mustn't and don't have to, and try the British Council exercises.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar memberi saran yang baik dan membicarakan aturan dalam bahasa Inggris. Yuk, mulai!

steps.title: Saran yang baik: should
steps.text: Kalau kamu bilang *sebaiknya …* ke teman, bahasa Inggrisnya **should**.
steps.body:
Polanya: **should + kata kerja dasar** (kata kerja seperti di kamus: tanpa -s, tanpa -ing, tanpa to). **You should drink more water.** Untuk ide yang buruk, pakai **shouldn't** (= should not): **You shouldn't stay up late.**
should adalah kata bantu seperti *can*: tidak pernah berubah, dan tidak ada apa-apa di antara should dan kata kerjanya. Jadi **she should go**, bukan 'she shoulds go' atau 'she should to go'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari capek sekali setelah seharian di kantor. Apa saran yang baik untuknya?

options: Sari should to go to bed early.
Sari shoulds go to bed early.
Sari should go to bed early.
question.explanation: **should + kata kerja dasar**: should go. Tidak ada **to** sesudah should, dan should tidak pernah diberi -s, walaupun subjeknya Sari (= she).

steps.title: Aturan dan kewajiban: have to dan must
steps.text: Kalau sesuatu **perlu** dilakukan (*harus, wajib*), bahasa Inggris memakai **have to** atau **must**.
steps.body:
**have to** + kata kerja dasar berubah seperti kata kerja *have* yang sudah kamu kenal: **I / you / we / they have to**, tapi **he / she has to** (seperti *she has a car*). Jadi 'she have to' itu salah.
**must** + kata kerja dasar tidak pernah berubah, seperti can: **I must, she must**, tanpa to sesudahnya.
Keduanya berarti *harus*. **have to** paling sering dipakai saat bicara; **must** sering muncul di papan tanda dan aturan tertulis.

steps.title: have to atau has to?
steps.text: Pak Hasan seorang satpam di sebuah bank di Surabaya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan ___ work at night on Fridays.
question.explanation: Pak Hasan = he, jadi **has to** (seperti *he has*). 'have to' untuk I / you / we / they, dan sesudah must tidak pernah ada **to**.

steps.title: Susun aturannya
steps.text: Sebuah kantor baru punya aturan untuk semua tamu. Resepsionis memberi tahu aturannya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kamu harus menunjukkan KTP-mu.
question.solution: You must show your ID card.
question.explanation: **must + kata kerja dasar**, tanpa to: **You must show** … Lalu apa yang ditunjukkan: **your ID card**.

steps.title: mustn't atau don't have to?
steps.text: Hati-hati! Dalam kalimat **negatif**, must dan have to artinya sangat berbeda.
steps.body:
**mustn't** (= must not) = *dilarang, tidak boleh*: ada aturan, atau berbahaya.
**don't have to** = *tidak perlu, tidak harus*: tidak wajib, kamu boleh memilih. Untuk he / she: **doesn't have to** (bukan 'doesn't has to').
Jebakannya: kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, *tidak harus* kelihatannya 'must not'. Padahal **mustn't** artinya *dilarang*! *Tidak harus / tidak perlu* = **don't have to**.

steps.title: Dilarang atau tidak perlu?
steps.text: Perhatikan contoh-contoh ini. Tanya dirimu: ini aturan, atau hanya tidak perlu?
steps.body: Aturan, papan tanda dan bahaya → **mustn't**. Barang gratis, hari libur, pilihan → **don't / doesn't have to**.

examples.en: You mustn't use your phone in the exam.
You mustn't touch the cables. It's dangerous.
The seminar is free. You don't have to pay.
examples.id: Seminarnya gratis. Kamu tidak perlu bayar.

examples.en: Sari doesn't have to cook tonight. Her mother is cooking.
examples.id: Sari tidak perlu masak malam ini. Ibunya sedang masak.

examples.en: Come to my house on Sunday! You don't have to bring anything.
examples.id: Datang ke rumahku hari Minggu! Tidak usah bawa apa-apa.

steps.title: Pagi yang santai
steps.text: Rina kerja di kantor dari Senin sampai Jumat. Hari ini hari Minggu.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: It's Sunday. Rina ___ get up early today.
question.explanation: Bangun pagi tidak dilarang; hari ini hanya tidak perlu, jadi **doesn't have to**. Rina = she, jadi **doesn't**. 'mustn't' artinya dia dilarang bangun pagi.

steps.title: Baca papannya
steps.text: Kamu di kolam renang di Bandung. Di dinding ada papan: **NO RUNNING**.

options: You don't have to run here.
question.explanation: Papan berisi aturan artinya tidak boleh: **mustn't** (= dilarang). 'You don't have to run' hanya berarti tidak perlu berlari.

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Ucapkan bahasa Inggrisnya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk saat kamu memberi saran atau membaca papan tanda!
